title: Sustainable linked harvest
stem: A two-region resource follows $s_{n+1}=As_n$, where $A=\begin{pmatrix}0.82&0.22\\0.22&0.82\end{pmatrix}$. After natural growth, a fixed fraction $h$ of each regional amount is removed. Unless otherwise stated, give numerical answers exactly or to three significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the new transition matrix and find its eigenvalues in terms of $h$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the harvest fraction for which the dominant eigenvalue is exactly 1.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain the long-term behaviour when $h$ is slightly below and slightly above this value.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Initially $s_0=(120,80)^T$. Find the limiting state at the threshold and discuss one limitation.

steps.text: Below this value, the dominant eigenvalue exceeds 1, so a positive symmetric component grows.
Above this value, both eigenvalue magnitudes are below 1 and amounts tend to zero.
At the threshold the symmetric component remains while the difference component decays.
The model permits fractional amounts and assumes constant reproduction and movement, which may fail at low stocks.
A dominant eigenvalue of 1 is a mathematical balance, not a guarantee against random depletion.
